statement: ReplicaStateMachine is the sole lifecycle owner for each partition-replica services row, and its handoff to ReplicaRemovalDurableCleanup is linearized on one exact durable generation: every existing-row lifecycle update is an UPDATE guarded by service_id, source status, and the source row's state_entered_at, or updated_at only for an observed legacy row without state_entered_at; an explicit non-apply or zero-row result cannot advance local state; an outcome-unknown REMOVING write fences every non-removal successor until an authoritative point observation proves the intended generation or a same-intent idempotent redrive resolves it; restart and stale or same-state ABA evidence carry their observed generation into the same CAS; canonical partition-leader settlement is confirmed or remains retry debt before services-row deletion or runtime retirement; and only that settled REMOVING generation may terminalize, while repeated completion and already-absent rows are idempotent and never recreate lifecycle authority.

constraints.statement: ReplicaStateMachine owns services lifecycle state; ReplicaRemovalDurableCleanup consumes its settled REMOVING outcome before deletion and local cleanup. FAILED, recovery, timeout handling, cache hydration, and ReplicaHandler may not become alternate lifecycle or cleanup authorities.

Every transition of an existing services row is a primary-key UPDATE whose predicate includes service_id, the admitted source status, and the observed source generation timestamp. Cache absence never authorizes UPSERT; initial creation and the explicit persist:false local fallback remain separate contracts.

Only a confirmed durable apply or an authoritative observation of the exact intended generation may commit local lifecycle state. Deferred, malformed, unknown, or zero-row mutation outcomes remain typed retry debt and never manufacture a local transition.

After a REMOVING write whose acknowledgement is lost, no FAILED, recovery, hydration, timeout, clear, or same-ID incarnation may cross the uncertainty fence. Resolution uses the canonical authoritative read path or an idempotent REMOVING redrive, never cached inference.

The existing conditional canonical partition-leader clear must be confirmed, or retained as reconstructible debt, before services-row deletion, runtime retirement, success emission, or local terminal completion. The Quest does not invent a second leader writer.

Only the same durable REMOVING generation with settled leader debt may become terminal. A stale recovery row, a different generation, or a non-REMOVING state cannot terminalize; repeated cleanup and authoritative absence are idempotent and never recreate the row.

The witnesses cover queued and synchronous re-entry, process restart after an applied write with lost acknowledgement, stale-cache recovery, same-state ABA, and repeated terminal redrive through production owner paths.

Each load-bearing production mechanism has a deterministic red-on-revert witness. No timeout or budget is widened, no assertion becomes eventual, no adversarial case is removed, and no ratchet baseline is raised.

This Quest repairs only the durable-generation and removal-settlement mechanism exposed by final verification. The five previously approved repair families remain frozen unless this witness or an exact-head gate demonstrates a new causal mechanism.
